commands.name: run
commands.summary: Execute the currently selected .bline module or a one-off command immediately.
commands.details:
Runs the currently active configuration or .bline module immediately.
This command triggers execution without saving any new state or changes.
Ideal for quick testing or one-shot workflows that don’t require persistence.

commands.name: use
commands.summary: Temporarily load one or more .bline modules for immediate use.
commands.details:
Loads .bline modules into memory for temporary use within the current session.
Accepts file paths or numeric indexes retrieved from the `list` command.
Modules loaded this way remain active until the session ends or another configuration is loaded.

commands.name: load
commands.summary: Persistently load a .bline module into session storage.
commands.details:
Loads a .bline module into persistent session memory, keeping it available until explicitly unloaded.
Useful for reusing common module chains or work environments across multiple runs.

commands.name: import
commands.summary: Import a .bline file into the local database for later use.
commands.details:
Stores an external .bline file in the local workspace database.
Imported modules can be referenced by name or index via the `list` and `use` commands.
Optionally supports overwrite behavior if a file already exists in the database.

commands.name: export
commands.summary: Export a stored .bline file to a given path.
commands.details:
Writes a stored .bline module to disk for sharing or backup.
If no destination is provided, the file will be written to the user’s home directory by default.
Accepts either a module ID or name for lookup.

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List items in the current context.
commands.details:
Displays loaded modules, saved workchains, payloads, tools, or historical data depending on the active context.
Used frequently to enumerate available resources for use or modification.

commands.name: edit
commands.summary: Open a .bline file in the configured editor.
commands.details:
Opens the specified .bline file for modification.
If the file does not exist, the system prompts to create a new one.
Supports both inline and external editors based on configuration.

commands.name: delete
commands.summary: Delete a .bline file from disk or the local database.
commands.details:
Removes a .bline module from the filesystem or the local workspace database.
Supports both file paths and numeric indexes. Confirmation may be required unless forced deletion is specified.

commands.name: reset
commands.summary: Reset the current environment and clear all loaded data.
commands.details:
Resets all environment variables, globals, and currently loaded modules.
Used to return the shell to a clean, default state without restarting the process.

commands.name: clear
commands.details:
Clears the console display.
Does not affect program state, configuration, or command history.

commands.name: update
commands.summary: Update modules, blocks, or core components.
commands.details:
Checks for and applies updates to system components, command definitions, or tool chains.
May perform network operations depending on configuration.
User confirmation is typically required before applying major updates.

commands.name: history
commands.summary: Manage and query build or execution history.
commands.details:
Provides access to past runs, builds, or workflows stored in local history.
Can list all entries, search for specific ones, or clear stored history entirely.
Filters and search terms are supported.

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Show current Blackline version and environment information.
commands.details:
Displays the current Blackline version number, environment details, and system configuration.
Useful for debugging or verifying compatibility with modules and workspace files.

commands.name: help
commands.summary: Show help information for commands or tools.
commands.details:
Displays a list of all commands, tools, and operators available within the environment.
When provided a command name, displays full details including syntax, arguments, and examples.

commands.name: exit
commands.details:
Terminates the current Blackline session.
Automatically saves session data and performs cleanup if enabled in configuration.
Can also be invoked with the alias `quit`.
